- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.2) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to capture mean reversion.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use 3-period moving average.  
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.6), model often fails to adjust quickly; apply lag correction: delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 periods.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts early in the cycle (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for first 7 days.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.6) and history shows low volatility, model tends to overfit recent trends; use 3-period smoothed average instead of raw forecast.
